decisions.old_assertion: HTTP success and the expected identity phrase in Markdown body
decisions.new_assertion: HTTP success AND the complete current English documentation-purpose sentence in Markdown body AND the exact expected identity in canonical metadata.title
decisions.intended_capability: Correct ordinary static-page content and identity, with body and title/metadata handled as separate normalized document fields (SPEC 31.1 and AC03)
decisions.intent_authority: Original row page_class=static plus canonical static-content/metadata assertions; no preserved instruction or pre-freeze source establishes a title-to-body insertion requirement
decisions.why_not_retrieval_failure: The expected title is returned in metadata and the current visible source purpose text is present in returned Markdown; missing title duplication does not demonstrate lost body content
decisions.why_not_easier: Metadata alone cannot pass. The replacement still requires nonempty actual body content, now a longer source-backed body assertion, and additionally requires exact metadata title. Wrong title, empty body, title-only body or missing source-purpose content all fail.
decisions.source_change_since_freeze: UNKNOWN; no pre-freeze HTML was retained. Do not label this as a proven later source change.
decisions.language_variant: The independent HTTPS response is English-only (577 bytes), while the historical browser HTML includes translations (2373 bytes). Both place identity in title and contain the same English body-purpose sentence.
